chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:

The waiting period of Mut'a is forty-five days. It is as if I am looking at Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) counting with his hand forty-five. So when the term passes, there is separation without a divorce.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for temporary marriage (Mut'a) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the 'iddah of Mut'a as forty-five days, with the narrator Zurrara vividly recalling Imam al-Baqir (AS) physically counting the days to emphasize the precision of this ruling. It clarifies that the contract terminates automatically upon expiration, distinguishing it from permanent marriage which requires a formal talaq for dissolution. This ruling is central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the temporary nature of Mut'a and the rights of the woman during the waiting period.
